description: Cross-platform golden vectors for the universal-v2 backup adapters (issue #277). The modeNormalization rows were hand-authored in commit 1a against the SHIPPING native code — Windows UniversalBackupMapper.MapToMode (+ CloudTranscriptionModels.ResolveModelAlias and CloudSttCatalog.NormalizeCloudProvider) and Linux ApplicationBackupService.ParseMode — so the Rust port in commit 1b can be diffed against them on the same inputs. A row with a single "expected" is one where the two heads AGREE today. A row carrying "expectedWindows" and "expectedLinux" records a drift that ships right now: Linux runs no cloud-routing migration, no catalog provider normalization, no model-alias resolution and no domain gate at all. Those rows collapse to a single "expected" in 1b; rows with one "expected" must not move.

modeNormalization.name: absent: a mode carrying no cloud-routing keys at all
modeNormalization.note: Trap #4. Every absent field must come out at the CALLER's own default (Mode.cs field initialisers), never at the core default (deepgramNova3 / grok:grok-4.3).

modeNormalization.name: absent: every cloud-routing key present but explicitly JSON null
modeNormalization.note: JSON null must behave exactly like an absent key on both heads.

modeNormalization.name: tier canonical id passes through unchanged
tier canonical id is matched case-insensitively
tier unknown value falls back to the core default
tier is surrounded by whitespace (Rust trims, C# present-guard does not)
tier is whitespace only
modeNormalization.note: Windows' MigrateCloudAccuracyTierPresent treats whitespace as absent and keeps the entity default; Linux stores the whitespace verbatim.

modeNormalization.name: cloudPostProcessingModel unknown single token falls back
cloudPostProcessingModel is whitespace only
modeNormalization.note: Present-only guard on Windows keeps the entity default rather than forcing the core fallback.

modeNormalization.name: qualified pp model: engine casing is canonicalised
qualified pp model: engine casing is canonicalised (anthropic)
qualified pp model: engine casing is canonicalised (cerebras)
qualified pp model: already-canonical engine passes through verbatim
modeNormalization.note: The model id is NOT validated against the catalog — a known engine passes the whole value through.

modeNormalization.name: qualified pp model: unknown model id under a known engine is still kept
qualified pp model: UNKNOWN engine falls through to the legacy switch and hits the fallback
qualified pp model: unknown engine whose suffix IS a legacy token still hits the fallback
modeNormalization.note: The legacy switch matches the WHOLE trimmed string, not the part after the colon.

modeNormalization.name: cloudProvider legacy alias "microsoftazurespeech" folds onto hyperwhisper + azureMaiTranscribe
modeNormalization.note: The folded tier lands on the mode ONLY because this mode carries no cloudAccuracyTier of its own — see vec-066 for the case where it does, and loses. This applies to the other plain-fold rows too (vec-063/064/065/067/075).

modeNormalization.name: cloudProvider legacy alias "microsoftAzureSpeech" folds onto hyperwhisper + azureMaiTranscribe
cloudProvider legacy alias "googlespeech" folds onto hyperwhisper + googleChirp3
cloudProvider legacy alias "googleSpeech" folds onto hyperwhisper + googleChirp3
cloudProvider fold: the mode's OWN cloudAccuracyTier BEATS the folded provider tier
modeNormalization.note: The object initializer really is `normalizedCloudProvider.AccuracyTier ?? migrated(universal) ?? Mode default`, so the fold wins THERE — but MapToMode then assigns CloudAccuracyTier a second time, unconditionally, from whichever post-initializer arm it takes. With no platformExtensions.windows it takes the else arm, `migrated(universal.CloudAccuracyTier) ?? mode.CloudAccuracyTier`, and MigrateCloudAccuracyTierPresent returns null ONLY for a null/blank input (an unknown value falls back to deepgramNova3, never to null). So any present tier overwrites the fold. Here 'high' is a real migrateFrom alias of deepgramNova3, so azureMaiTranscribe is discarded. The fold survives only when the arm's own tier source is absent or blank.

modeNormalization.name: cloudProvider fold: a legacy model id is NOT aliased, because ResolveModelAlias sees the RAW provider
modeNormalization.note: MapToMode passes universal.CloudProvider (raw), not the normalized provider, to FromIdentifier — so the azure branch hits the passthrough arm.

modeNormalization.name: BYOK passthrough: "deepgram" is a tier alias but NOT a provider alias — it must not fold
modeNormalization.note: deepgram appears in TIER_ALIASES for accuracy-tier migration; legacyCloudProviderAliases is kept separate exactly so BYOK provider names survive.

modeNormalization.name: BYOK passthrough: "groq" is a tier alias but NOT a provider alias
BYOK passthrough: "elevenlabs" is a tier alias but NOT a provider alias
BYOK passthrough: a deepgram mode with a legacy model id still resolves the model
domain gate: hyperwhisper keeps the domain
domain gate: a BYOK provider DROPS the domain on Windows
domain gate: an absent provider DROPS the domain on Windows
domain gate: a folded provider keeps the domain, because the fold happens first
domain gate: hyperwhisper with no domain stays absent
model alias table is matched case-insensitively
model alias: a current id passes through unchanged
model alias: a provider with no alias table passes the model through
model alias: hyperwhisper is NOT one of the five tables, so a legacy id is kept
model alias: the empty model id survives as the empty string
modeNormalization.note: Grok registers its single entry under id "" — ResolveModelAlias short-circuits on IsNullOrEmpty.

modeNormalization.name: unknown provider: FromIdentifier returns None, so ALL FIVE tables are chained (elevenlabs)
unknown provider: chain resolves an assemblyai id
unknown provider: chain resolves a deepgram id
unknown provider: chain resolves a soniox id
unknown provider: chain resolves a gemini id
unrecognised provider string: kept verbatim, but the model still goes through the chain
empty provider string: echoed back as the empty string, not null
modeNormalization.note: normalize_cloud_provider filters on !is_empty and returns the ORIGINAL Option, so "" round-trips as "".

modeNormalization.name: platformExtensions.windows.cloudAccuracyTier overrides the universal value
modeNormalization.note: Windows re-applies the extension value AFTER the universal one; Linux reads platformExtensions.linux and never sees this slice.

modeNormalization.name: platformExtensions.windows present but carrying no tier: the universal value survives
modeNormalization.note: Present-only again — an extension slice without the key must not overwrite with a default.

modeNormalization.name: platformExtensions.windows tier BEATS the folded tier; the fold still owns cloudProvider
modeNormalization.note: The winExt arm of MapToMode. cloudProvider stays folded to hyperwhisper — nothing in platformExtensions can undo that — but the tier does not stay folded: `migrated(winExt.CloudAccuracyTier) ?? mode.CloudAccuracyTier` migrates 'medium' to groqWhisper and discards azureMaiTranscribe. Note this arm does NOT re-read universal.CloudAccuracyTier, so when winExt carries no tier the folded tier is what survives — that is the one place the initializer's `normalizedCloudProvider.AccuracyTier ??` is load-bearing.

modeNormalization.name: a foreign (macos) per-mode slice does not affect cloud routing
legacy azure standalone mode: provider and domain fold, but its own cloudAccuracyTier survives
modeNormalization.note: Same rule as vec-066, on a fully-populated legacy mode. The provider folds to hyperwhisper (which in turn opens the domain gate, so 'medical' is kept), but the mode's own 'medium' is migrated to groqWhisper and overwrites the folded azureMaiTranscribe in the post-initializer else arm. This is NOT the 'full fold' the old label claimed: a legacy azure mode that carries any tier of its own lands on that tier, not on azureMaiTranscribe.
